clue.text: Many left town

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword stand-in for many
left in the sense of remaining, as in food left over

explanation.surface: Lots of people have moved out of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is the English Channel port town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is a port in Kent, an example of an English settlement of that kind.

clue.text: "Look", a new paper

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of paper are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone points out a newly launched newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns PAPER into PPEAR, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To look a certain way is to seem or give that impression, a synonym.

clue.text: Criminal fool-the fool yet again inside

parts.note: an ass is a silly person, a fool
a second ass, repeating the fool
inside means in

explanation.surface: A crook who is a double idiot ends up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer is a kind of lawbreaker, so an example of a criminal.

clue.text: Opposite, poetically expressed

explanation.surface: Something said contrary, but put in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is IN VERSE, written as poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite: reversed in order or relation, a mathematical term; poetically expressed: written in metre and rhyme, split as two words.

clue.text: The way a guide is found for the newcomer

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a Ranger is a senior member of the Girl Guides movement in Britain

explanation.surface: A street is where a scout leader welcomes someone new.
explanation.walkthrough: In British Guiding, Rangers are the oldest section of the Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: A person new to a place is unknown there, a synonym for an arrival.

clue.text: Keeps quiet over books

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places one piece on top of the next

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A librarian keeps silence over the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something is to save or maintain it, as with jam or a nature reserve.

clue.text: Settling for writing notes

explanation.surface: Calming down so as to jot something down.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling: calming oneself or arranging a dispute; writing notes: creating music on the stave.

clue.text: Back rents to be collected

indicators.note: collected suggests the letters of rents are gathered up and re-sorted

explanation.surface: A landlord must collect overdue rent payments.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear part of a ship is its back end, so a synonym in nautical use.

clue.text: A woman five are backing up

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: backing up in a down clue means the word are is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Five people support one woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing up' turns ARE into ERA, after V.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a female first name, so an example of a lady.

clue.text: Refuse to allow a seamstress very much time

parts.note: a seamstress is one who sews, a sew-er
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone declines to give a dressmaker plenty of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, waste. SEWER here is one who sews, not a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainage waste is rubbish carried away, a synonym for the noun meaning waste.

clue.text: Turning pale, points to pass

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of pale are spun into another order

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Someone going white while points of time slip by.
explanation.definitionFit: When time goes by it slips away, a synonym for to pass.

clue.text: The girl in a fair-isle jumper

indicators.note: in tells us the girl's name sits inside the word fair-isle

explanation.surface: A girl wearing a patterned Fair Isle knitted sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A Fair Isle jumper is a patterned knitted sweater from the Shetland isle of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a female first name, an example of a woman's name.

clue.text: Get grass dealt with, and that causes astonishment

indicators.note: dealt with suggests the letters of get grass are handled and reshuffled like cards

explanation.surface: Someone told to sort out the lawn is amazed.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze someone is to stun or bowl them over, a synonym.

clue.text: The ebbing tide?

parts.note: a tide that ebbs is sea water going down, so a whimsical name for a cascade

explanation.surface: A question about the sea going out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a stream dropping over a cliff, the water falling as the tide does.

clue.text: Stick around longing for hot stuff

indicators.note: around tells us the stick goes round the longing

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
a yen is a yearning, a longing

explanation.surface: A walking stick wrapped around a craving for something spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a fiery red pepper, an example of a spicy seasoning.

clue.text: Recent disquiet about an actress's appearance

indicators.note: about tells us the jumbled letters go around an
disquiet suggests the letters of recent are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An actress has recently been anxious about her stage debut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disquiet' rearranges RECENT into ENTRCE, which goes 'about' AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's arrival on stage is her coming on, a theatrical synonym.

clue.text: He'll get on-confidently expects to get somewhere

definitions.text: He'll get on-confidently expects to get somewhere

parts.words: He'll get on-confidently expects to get somewhere
parts.note: sounds like an ambitious person, but describes a passenger stepping on to a bus or ship to travel

explanation.surface: A go-getter sure of success.
explanation.definitionFit: One who boards a vessel or bus is a passenger, getting on to travel to a destination.

clue.text: An opening for a music man

definitions.text: An opening for a music man

parts.words: An opening for a music man
parts.note: sounds like a job vacancy for a musician, but means an orchestral introduction

explanation.surface: A job vacancy for a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestral prelude introduces an opera or concert, the music's start.

clue.text: Irritated when required to accept cash

indicators.note: to accept tells us the needed word takes in the cash

parts.note: required means needed
L is the symbol for a pound, a sum of cash

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at being made to take payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To be needled is to be annoyed or provoked, a synonym.

clue.text: Just a few words in condemnation of the wrongdoer

explanation.surface: A judge's brief pronouncement condemning a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Just a few words: a grammatical unit, a short string of words; condemnation of the wrongdoer: the punishment a judge passes.

clue.text: Some fine royal robes fit for an emperor

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Splendid royal garments suitable for a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'robes fit for', but the four letters need only 'emperor'; 'robes fit for an' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman ruler of the first century, an example of an imperial ruler.

clue.text: Feel jealous of a minister who lacks nothing

indicators.note: lacks tells us the minister is missing the nothing

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic minister
O is nothing, the figure zero

explanation.surface: Resent a diplomat who has nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet what another has is to begrudge it, a synonym.

clue.text: Disappear if a vehicle is "hot"!

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
taken as written
H is hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Get away quickly if the van is stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' in the surface means stolen, which fits a getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to go out of sight, a synonym.

clue.text: Speak without qualification

explanation.surface: Talk freely, with no conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Speak: to say or voice words; without qualification: absolute, as in complete nonsense.

clue.text: A really loud tune can give rise to some concern

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, very loud in music
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A loud song may cause worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter or business is one's concern, a synonym as in 'that's my business'.

clue.text: Set off only to end in confusion and scoffed

indicators.note: in confusion means the letters of to end are muddled into a new order

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed means ate

explanation.surface: Someone set out only to finish muddled and mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confusion' rearranges TO END into DETON. 'scoffed' looks like mocked but means ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to explode it, a synonym.

clue.text: A quarter need to relax

parts.note: S, south, is one quarter of the compass
lack is need or want

explanation.surface: Part of a community must unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen or ease off is to let go, a synonym.

clue.text: He's put right about gear with a certain hesitation

parts.note: re means about, concerning
gear is clothing, dress
er is a hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Someone put straight about clothes, but with some hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rectifies a wrong is a remedier, as in seeking redress.
